domain: forced displacement - annual country-of-origin refugee population (international organisation publisher; UNICEF's SDMX republishing of UNHCR statistics)
prediction_question: Hypothetical task this source would support (parked on split capacity, not formulated further): for a country of origin with at least 1,000 refugees and other people in need of international protection abroad at end of year D, will that population grow by more than 25% in year D+1?
prediction_time: Would be the publication of the year-D value in UNICEF's MG series (annual data for year D appears during D+1; the SDMX rows carry no vintage field, so as-of reproducibility under UNHCR revisions is an open construction question).
target_definition: Would be binary from the year-D+1 row's OBS_VALUE of the same origin: (OBS_VALUE[D+1] > 1.25 x OBS_VALUE[D]) with OBS_VALUE[D] >= 1000. Label source column: the TIME_PERIOD=D+1 OBS_VALUE, excluded from shipped features. Unit: persons. Frame: UNICEF MG_RFGS_CNTRY_ORIGIN, AGE=_T, country ISO3 REF_AREA only (155 aggregate REF_AREAs excluded).

license_evidence.note: HDX dataset record for unicef-mg-rfgs-cntry-origin (read 2026-10-20 via the CKAN package_show API): license_title = 'CC BY 3.0 IGO'. UNICEF publishes its data under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 IGO; attribution-only, no NC/ND restriction, redistribution of derived rows permitted with citation. The underlying statistics are UNHCR's (the DATA_SOURCE field on every row cites 'United Nations High Commissioner for Refugeers, Global Trends: Forced Displacement in 2025. UNHCR, 2026.'), so any release must attribute both UNICEF (publisher of this view) and UNHCR (source of the statistics).

measurements.full_download_2026_10_20: GET https://sdmx.data.unicef.org/ws/public/sdmxapi/rest/data/UNICEF,MG,1.0/.MG_RFGS_CNTRY_ORIGIN.?format=csv -> HTTP 200, 4,967 KiB, 12,452 rows, 0.5 s, single request from the coordinator.
measurements.table_shape_2026_10_20: 12,452 rows = 364 REF_AREAs x years 2001-2025 x AGE split. AGE=_T: 8,475 rows (OBS_STATUS empty); AGE=Y0T17 (children 0-17): 3,977 rows, ALL with OBS_STATUS='MD' (missing/magnitude-unknown in this pull - the child-age disaggregation is not usable). 155 REF_AREAs are aggregates (UNICEF_WCA, WPP_GLOBAL, AU_AFRICA, FAO_LIFDC...) and were excluded, leaving 209 country origins. SOURCE_LINK on every row points back at https://www.unhcr.org/refugee-statistics/download/ - this series is UNICEF's republishing of the UNHCR RDF data.
measurements.split_window_counts_2026_10_20: Country-only, AGE=_T, base population >= 1000, growth>25% into D+1 - computed from the downloaded table: train 2001-2015: 1,356 origin-years, 155 positives (11.4%) across 72 distinct surging origins; eval 2016-2019: 378 origin-years, 34 positives (9.0%) across 22 distinct surging origins; holdout 2020-2024: 485 origin-years, 72 positives (14.8%) across 44 distinct surging origins. Both classes present in every window, but the clustered effective sample (surging origins) is thin: 22 in the eval window.

rejection_reason: PARK (status parked), reason: split capacity, not access or licence - both of those are good and are recorded so they are not re-probed. (1) The clustered effective sample is too thin for a scored binary eval: positives are surge situations, and the eval window carries only 34 positive origin-years across 22 distinct surging origins (holdout: 72 across 44). A 378-row eval split with 34 positives cannot carry a stable AUC, and the confidence interval on 22 clustered events is the honest sample size. (2) The series is UNHCR-derived (DATA_SOURCE cites UNHCR Global Trends; SOURCE_LINK points at the RDF), so building here would publish a thinner derivative of the source whose richer parent record (unhcr-refugee-data-finder) is access-parked - the bench would gain no genuinely new data. Prior-art comparison recorded in notes (no ML-ready equivalent exists, but that does not rescue the sample size).
next_action: Unpark condition (exact): a machine-fetchable richer grain of the same phenomenon - UNHCR RDF's monthly asylum applications or host-country x origin population series - at which point the task should be built on the UNHCR record (see unhcr-refugee-data-finder's unpark question), not on this annual derivative. This record stays the measured evidence that the UNICEF path itself works (anonymous SDMX, CC BY 3.0 IGO) but is annually thin; only reopen it if the operator explicitly wants the thin annual task despite the clustered-sample limitation. UPDATE 2026-10-23: the machine-fetchable richer grain now exists - the UNHCR record (unhcr-refugee-data-finder) was reopened and is ready with the corridor-grain annual asylum-applications task via the HDX global package (data.unhdata.org, dataset unhcr-population-data-for-world), which carries eval/holdout split capacity this annual derivative cannot (166 eval positives across 109 origin-year clusters vs 34 here). The richer task lives there; this record stays parked as the thin-derivative evidence and does not need re-probing.
